sense: the look of the land, scenery

terms.gloss: the look of a place, its landscape
evidence: Tac. Ann. 4.67: faciem locī verteret (Lewis & Short, s.v. faciēs)
terms.comment: Latin speaks of the look (faciēs), the lie (situs) or the loveliness (amoenitās) of a place, or simply of the places (loca), rather than of a landscape. faciēs is first the face, and then any outward form or appearance (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: lovely scenery, the charm of a place
terms.comment: Loveliness, “in general of objects affecting the sense of sight” (Lewis & Short, s.v. amoenus): of gardens, rivers and coasts. loca amoena (Varro, Sallust) are pleasant places, lovely scenery.
Traupman’s phrase. regiō is a district or region, fōrma a shape; for a view from a height see view.
Only of landscapes painted on walls; a landscape gardener is a topiārius (Cic.; M-O).

phrases.latin: cum locīs ipsīs dēlectēmur, montuōsīs etiam et silvestribus, in quibus diūtius commorātī sumus
phrases.english: since we take pleasure in places themselves, even mountainous and wooded ones, where we have stayed for a long time

phrases.latin: ex propinquō vīsa montium altitūdō nivēsque caelō prope immixtae
phrases.english: the height of the mountains, seen from close by, and the snows almost blending with the sky

phrases.latin: in Arpīnātī summā cum amoenitāte, tum salūbritāte flūminis mē refēcī
phrases.english: at Arpinum I recovered by the river, in the loveliest and healthiest of places

sources: Lewis & Short: facies · Lewis & Short: amoenitas · Lewis & Short: amoenus · Lewis & Short: regio · Lewis & Short: topia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 337. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. scenery; forms: landscape.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-livius, loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there. Tacitus as Lewis & Short quotes him.
